traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements of docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md are fully implemented and verified by targeted tests.
• Core Functionality & User Experience: Every relevant rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) defines clear, specific meta.messages and uses context.report with structured data so diagnostics state exactly what is wrong and how to fix it. Tests assert on messageId and data contents, including function names, paths, requirement IDs, and human-readable details.
• Error Message Conventions & Consistency: The message patterns described in the story (function identifiers, branch missingAnnotation with {{missing}}, format messages using {{details}}, file/req errors using {{path}}, {{reqId}}, {{storyPath}}) are all reflected in rule meta and enforced by tests. There is minor variation in placeholder naming (e.g., '{{name}}' vs '{{functionName}}' in one rule), but tests and data wiring ensure the intended information (function name) is present and consistent, and the story’s own 'Current Rule Implementations' section matches the actual templates.
• Error Suggestions: For require-story-annotation, the story’s focus for ESLint suggestions, tests explicitly verify that suggestions exist, have clear descriptions, and provide example annotations. Other rules provide actionable guidance via their message text even when they do not use the suggest API.
• Error Location & Integration: All rules report against the appropriate AST node; function rules include the function name in data, and comment-based rules include exact offending path/ID. Tests assert the data contents, ensuring ESLint will display rich, contextual messages integrated with standard tooling.
• Error Handling: valid-story-reference and supporting utilities cleanly distinguish missing files from filesystem errors, surfacing fileAccessError with error details rather than throwing. The plugin index file provides robust handling for rule-load failures using a fallback rule with explicit diagnostics. Corresponding tests confirm these behaviors.
• Severity Mapping: src/index.ts encodes the story’s severity conventions (errors for missing annotations/references, warnings for format issues) in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and applies them in the recommended and strict flat configs. Tests validate this mapping.
Given the direct traceability annotations, comprehensive rule coverage, and fully passing, story-specific test suites, this story is fully implemented and remains in a passing state.
